extracted.intended_audience: research administrators and higher-education faculty (especially College of Education faculty) interested in faculty grant-writing support
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based study identifying which motivators and barriers to grant writing College of Education faculty perceive as important, comparing tenured and non-tenured respondents and offering institutional recommendations to increase grant-writing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to probe or research new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty-rated motivator: the chance to explore new research questions or information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the top motivator (mean = 2.61 on 0–3 importance scale for both tenured and non-tenured faculty). Emphasizes that proposals oriented to new inquiry are motivating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support when proposals are funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel support such as graduate assistants and clerical help available when proposals are funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated highly as a motivator (mean = 2.59). Faculty cited the value of funded project staffing and clerical support for conducting funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Having travel money available for conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of travel funds to attend conferences tied to grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated a motivator (mean = 2.26). Travel monies were recommended among incentives to encourage grant-seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building professional reputation as a capable researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Using grant activity to enhance one's research reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated a motivator (mean = 2.26) and noted as a common motivator across different institution types (also found in Boyer & Cockriel, 1998).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support when preparing proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of graduate assistants or clerical help during proposal preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated a motivator (mean = 2.21). Faculty specifically valued assistance during the time-intensive proposal-writing phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: More flexibility in how time is allocated
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility in teaching/service assignments or workload to allow time for grant writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated a motivator (mean = 2.12). Recommendation: create a new formula for teaching/service/research to allow time for grant-skill development and procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance in grant proposal preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct help with writing and assembling grant proposals (e.g., administrative or editorial assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated a motivator (mean = 2.11). Faculty asked for streamlined review procedures and administrative assistance with proposal preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate support available to submit proposals in a timely manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: lack of institutional support/resources to prepare and submit proposals quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the single barrier with mean > 2 for both tenured and non-tenured faculty (mean = 2.18). Faculty described poor infrastructure, cumbersome procedures, and insufficient clerical help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy teaching load
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: large teaching responsibilities that reduce time to pursue grant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistically significant difference (p < .05) found: tenured faculty rated heavy teaching load as a more important barrier than non-tenured faculty (tenured mean 2.45 vs non-tenured 1.69). Recommendation: adjust workload allocations to permit grant activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Too many committee assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: excessive committee/service obligations interfering with grant-writing time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among barriers (ranked in Table 1). Implies institutional service loads can reduce capacity for grant-focused work.

rubrics_metrics.name: University culture not supportive of grant writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier/theme: institutional culture perceived as not rewarding or supporting grant-seeking (includes poor infrastructure and lack of rewards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative thematic finding: 14 of 22 open-ended respondents cited culture as a barrier, noting inadequate processes, lack of GA support, little return of indirects to departments, and scant recognition in promotion/tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate grant administrative process / infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: poor procedural systems for administering grants (e.g., too many required signatures, lack of clerical support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty described 'poor infrastructure,' cumbersome signature processes, and administrators absorbing support systems. Recommendation: provide a campus-wide system for administering grants, including clerical aid for procedural functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of rewards or recognition for grant procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: scarce institutional recognition or credit for grant work in promotion and tenure decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty reported 'Lack of recognition for grants through P & T' and questioned whether indirect funds benefit departments or faculty. Recommendation: include grant writing and procurement in tenure/promotion criteria and recognize grant procurement as scholarly work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of training in seeking and writing grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: insufficient training opportunities for faculty to learn grant-seeking and grant-writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified in Boyer & Cockriel (1998) and discussed as a known barrier; recommendation: provide instruction and professional development to enhance grant-writing skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge in budget development
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: faculty not knowing how to develop grant budgets effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a significant barrier in prior research (Boyer & Cockriel, 1998). Institutional budgeting assistance recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge regarding potential funding sources / contact with funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier/motivator: not knowing potential sponsors or lacking contact reduces proposals; contact with funding sources can be motivating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty mentioned funder contact as a possible motivator; lack of knowledge about funding sources was a barrier in prior studies. Recommendation: facilitate funder contact and awareness of funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect funds (return of indirects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration: availability and distribution of indirect funds from grants (how indirects are used/distributed affects faculty motivation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty complained that the university 'took all the indirects and gave nothing back' — perceived as demotivating. Recommendation: transparent, faculty-beneficial indirect distribution policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates / boilerplates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proposal templates or boilerplates to ease proposal writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original survey used the term 'boilerplates' (changed to 'templates' in this study to avoid confusion). Templates had modest means in Appendix A; inclusion can streamline proposal preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting funded (success as motivator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivator: the prospect or reality of obtaining funding for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although mean values varied, 'getting funded' is an intrinsic motivator and interacts with recognition, resources, and workload considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to equipment and research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivator: ability to obtain equipment or resources for students/research as a result of grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In open-ended responses, faculty cited acquiring equipment and research opportunities for students as motivating reasons to write grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivator: collaborative research enabled by grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration appeared in Appendix A; fostering collaborative teams and team-focused grants was noted as part of grant-writing's characteristics (Porter, 2007) and can motivate faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisement / mentoring in grant writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Support: mentorship or advisement from experienced colleagues in preparing proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A lists advisement as a factor; recommendations include instruction and fellowship programs (e.g., Banta et al., 2004) to cultivate skills among new faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-consuming / inconvenience of proposal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Barrier: perception that grant writing and administrative processes are time-consuming or inconvenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A lists 'time consuming' and 'inconvenience' among barriers. Streamlining processes and providing clerical support can reduce these burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced signatures / simplified approval workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative change: reducing the number of required signatures and simplifying approvals to expedite submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants recommended fewer required signatures; tied to the broader recommendation to improve administrative infrastructure for grant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a campus-wide system for administering grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: centralize and professionalize grant administration (grant writing assistance, budgeting assistance, clerical aid for procedural tasks like obtaining signatures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit recommendation from authors: a campus-wide support system would address many identified barriers (timeliness, paperwork, budgeting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide incentives for grant writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: offer incentives such as travel funds, flexibility in assignments, recognition for grant procurement, graduate assistants, and professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend concrete incentives to motivate faculty, reflecting items faculty rated as motivating (e.g., travel money, flexibility, GA support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide instruction to enhance grant writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: deliver training and professional development focused on grant-seeking and proposal writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the recurring barrier of lack of training; examples include fellowship-style programs and workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include grant writing in tenure and promotion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: formally recognize grant-writing activity in tenure and promotion decisions to motivate faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend including grant writing as part of P&T criteria and valuing procurement of various levels as significant scholarly work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust faculty workload formula to allow grant development time
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: create a new teaching/service/research formula that permits time for grant writing and skill development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses barriers such as heavy teaching load and too many committee assignments by reallocating time and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further assess faculty perceptions of institutional culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: conduct additional assessment of how institutional culture supports or inhibits grant-writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors suggest including organizational-culture items in future surveys to better target interventions; qualitative thematic analysis revealed culture as a major barrier.
